Bautista saved 33 games and struck out 110 in 61 innings while earning an All-Star nod in 2023, but he missed the final month of that season and all of 2024 while recovering from Tommy John surgery. He had 19 saves in 35 games in 2025 before surgery to repair his torn labrum and torn rotator cuff ended his season. Bautista had a 2.35 ERA in nine minor league rehab games. "He is as close to full go as he could be," manager Craig Albernaz said. "We're going to try to be as smart as we can with using Félix. But also, the game is chaotic and unpredictable, so you don't know what's going to happen." The Orioles also optioned pitcher Cade Povich and outfielder Heston Kjerstad to Triple-A Norfolk, activated outfielder Christian Franklin from the 10-day injured list and transferred outfielder Tyler O'Neill to the 60-day IL. Mike Elias, Baltimore's president of baseball operations, said Saturday that Albernaz would return in 2027. The Orioles are 75-79 in Albernaz's first season and began the day three games out of an American League wild-card spot. "It's a great vote of confidence," Albernaz said. "Obviously, this season hasn't gone the way I wanted it by any stretch, by how the players wanted the season to go, how the front office, how the fanbase. ... That's something I wear pretty heavily because of the seat I'm in and I don't take that lightly." In addition, Trey Mancini signed a one-day contract to retire with the Orioles, the franchise he played for during the bulk of his eight-year career in the majors. [Alysa Liu skipping '26-27 skating season to 'recalibrate'] Olympic gold medalist Alysa Liu announced she's taking the upcoming figure skating season off and plans to return in 2027-28. In a social media post Tuesday, Liu wrote that she's looking to "take the time to recalibrate." "I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve," she wrote, in part, on Instagram. "It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth. I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot. So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far. See yall soon!!" View this post on Instagram A post shared by 刘美贤 (@alysaxliu) Liu, 21, became the first American woman to win a Winter Games gold medal in more than two decades back in February in Milan and returned to the United States a national hero. She previously withdrew from this year's figure skating world championships a month after the Winter Games ended, a common occurrence for Olympic athletes. In an interview with NBC Sports , Liu said she'll spend the time off continuing to train and hone her skills. "I really want to improve my skating, and I wanted to take the time to do that for myself and just to evolve, and then I'll be back after that is done," she said in the interview. "But I'll still be cheering on all my competitors and my teammates, and I'm really excited." Liu had been scheduled to compete in the first leg of Skate America's Grand Prix in Everett, Washington on Nov. 13-15 before her announcement Tuesday.

Though he retired after the 2023-24 season, the allure of playing with Myles Garrett proved to be too much for the three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Donald returns on a one-year, $20 million contract with the Los Angeles Rams , ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday. Though the future Hall of Famer is the most recent prominent name to return to their sport after a notable break, he isn't the first. Some legendary figures have made their own comebacks over the years, with some enjoying impressive career second winds as well. Here are some of the other high-profile names Donald is joining. Likely the most famous return to a sport of all time, the simple tagline for Jordan's 1995 comeback -- "I'm back" -- is still referenced today. The Chicago Bulls superstar had been on a yearlong sojourn in baseball after having announced his NBA retirement in October 1993, but he rejoined the Bulls in the second half of the 1994-95 season. It didn't take long for Jordan's impact to be felt. In his first full season back, the Bulls returned to and won the NBA Finals, and Chicago would follow that up with two more consecutive titles in the following years for the second three-peat of Jordan's career. Jordan then retired again, from which he'd make another comeback three years later, playing two seasons with the Washington Wizards before his last and official retirement in 2003. One of the inspirations for Jordan's second comeback was the return of his friend Lemieux several months earlier. Lemieux announced his retirement from hockey in 1997 after eight All-Star nods and 1,494 career points under his belt, his production coming even with his 12-season career having been interrupted by a diagnosis of Hodgkin lymphoma (then known as Hodgkin's disease) in 1993.
